expect:

A) Mitochondria
B) Cell membrane
C) Nucleus
D) Chloroplasts
value:
Which one of the following is found in a bacterial cell but NOT in an animal cell?
A) Mitochondria
B) Plasmids
C) Nucleus
D) Chloroplasts
note: F1: the stem asks for a structure in bacteria but not animal cells; every option failed that test and the key named the cell membrane, which animal cells also have. Plasmids make the key correct.

expect:
B) Cell membrane [1 mark]

Note: Bacterial cells have a cell membrane (and a cell wall), but no mitochondria, no true nucleus and no chloroplasts. Animal cells have a cell membrane but no cell wall.
value:
B) Plasmids [1 mark]

Note: Plasmids are small rings of extra DNA found in prokaryotic cells such as bacteria. Animal cells never contain them. Bacterial cells also have no mitochondria, no true nucleus and no chloroplasts, and both cell types have a cell membrane.
note: F1: answer key corrected to match the repaired options.
